component_records.title: Project management, governance and reporting
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the study for MHTC and MoDOT under a 15-month contract period, with the work plan, schedule and resource loading finalised at kick-off and recognising MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. The component facilitates the kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review work plan, scope and schedule and to set the protocol for ongoing communications, and schedules and conducts quarterly project status meetings reviewing the previous period and the next. It produces minutes for the kick-off and every quarterly status meeting, submits quarterly written updates on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December, and maintains monthly e-mail and telephone contact with MoDOT contacts for ongoing progress updates. It coordinates all activities with the Construction and Materials Division and makes advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division as work progresses, and it consults MHTC's representative on any concerns about administration of the services. The work plan details implementation of every task in the scope of work with the resources and schedule required, and the project manager reports against it at each status meeting.

component_records.title: Data management plan and research data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of the kick-off meeting the team submits a Data Management Plan to MoDOT that describes the anticipated formats for the project data and related files, including the MHTC parameter extracts, the MoDOT-supplied example legal land descriptions, the training and test property sets, and the model outputs and review annotations. The plan commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats for the data and files that must remain usable after the study, so MoDOT can reuse the corpus and outputs without licence dependency. The plan also sets the retention, access and handover arrangements for the corpus at close-out, consistent with MHTC ownership of materials produced at its direction.

component_records.title: Literature review and practice scan
component_records.description: The team conducts a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practice in using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, vendor and pilot evidence, and peer state DOT programmes, and reports what worked, what failed and what accuracy and review effort those programmes achieved. The review is delivered as a written chapter of the interim and final reports and is used to fix the design choices for the prototype, including model approach, input parameter set and human review workflow. Findings are presented to MoDOT at the quarterly status meeting following completion so the Technical Advisory Committee can steer the proof of concept.

component_records.title: LLD rule set and MHTC parameter specification
component_records.description: The team converts the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 requirements and MHTC's description conventions into an explicit, testable rule set that the drafting tool applies. The rule set enforces the metes and bounds method for realty rights acquired or conveyed, the exact last-deed-of-record wording where a property is acquired in its entirety, and recital of the specific rights being acquired, conveyed or leased where those rights are less than fee simple, accurately described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls. The team documents the MHTC parameters the tool consumes, their form and source, and validates the rule set against MoDOT-supplied example descriptions before any prototype output is shown. The rule set is delivered as a configuration artefact and a chapter of the final report so MoDOT can maintain it after the study.

component_records.title: AI/ML LLD drafting prototype (build and configure)
component_records.description: The team builds and configures a web-based drafting application that generates a first draft legal land description from MHTC parameters, to determine the usefulness of AI and ML for that purpose. The application is developed on approved technologies: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release with the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework, in C#, JavaScript, CSS and HTML, with Python 3.x reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses and any larger Python use submitted to the IS Best Practices Review Team for approval. It runs as a browser-based application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, is tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, and its library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually. Where an on-premise database is needed it is deployed on Oracle 19C, with Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher proposed only if the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team approves it. The application stores no Personal Identifiable Information in any database table unless a specific business need is approved by the IS Cyber Security Team, meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, uses no third-party tool that places a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management approval, uses no third-party text, graphics or code without permission, and suppresses vendor logos and branding wherever a supported licensed option exists. The named LLD development program is submitted to MoDOT Information Systems for approval before Task 3c proceeds.

component_records.title: Proof of concept, demonstration and surveyor review loop
component_records.description: The team demonstrates on 4/25/2025 how its technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, using MoDOT-supplied example properties and MHTC parameters, and shows how MoDOT feedback is incorporated for improvement. MoDOT Right of Way staff review and edit each generated draft in the tool, and the team records edit effort and error types per property so the usefulness of the AI/ML first draft is evidenced rather than asserted. A professional land surveyor reviews every draft description to verify that the parcel described corresponds with the right-of-way plans and that the right-of-way plans correspond with the survey information gathered, and the review is completed before any deed document is presented to a grantor. The team then adjusts the tool against the review findings, and the adjusted build is the version trained on and handed over.

component_records.title: Training and user manual
component_records.description: After the tool adjustments are made, the team produces a user manual and delivers training to MoDOT Right of Way staff by 7/25/2025. The training covers how to load MHTC parameters, generate a first draft, review and edit it, and route it to the professional land surveyor, and the user manual is written as the reference staff use after the sessions, with the same steps, screens and worked examples. Training is delivered in person at a MoDOT location with a recorded virtual session for staff who cannot attend, and the manual is issued in an accessible electronic format plus printed copies for the Right of Way team. Attendance, materials and the manual are handed to the MoDOT project manager at completion.

component_records.title: Reporting, presentations and close-out
component_records.description: The team completes an interim presentation by 9/15/2025 covering progress, demonstration results and the plan for the remaining work, and submits the draft final report, research summary and user manual by 11/3/2025 for MoDOT review. It delivers the final report, 1-2 page research summary, presentation and user manual by 1/1/2026, with the final report detailing every task completed and all findings generated during the project, the summary stating project objectives, findings and conclusions, and the presentation summarising the significant details for MoDOT staff. Reports and the summary follow the Publication Guidelines and summary template published on the MoDOT information-for-researchers page, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page. The team submits the final invoice by 2/2/2026 when the contract ends, and hands over all documents, reports, exhibits and materials produced at MHTC's direction as MHTC property.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance workstream, led by a contracts manager reporting to the project manager, carries the obligations that sit outside the technical build. It holds the offer to provide the services at the fees quoted under the RFP terms and prices the full scope of services on the Section (4) Price Page cost estimate, broken into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, with Miscellaneous itemised on an attached sheet, within the $175,000 not-to-exceed amount. It accepts that proposals and related information are open to public inspection without reservation, that award is subject to a post-award negotiated contract on the RFP's stated provisions, and that MHTC may cancel the award and select another Offeror if terms cannot be agreed. It maintains the independent contractor position, assuming all legal and financial responsibility for taxes, FICA, fringe benefits, workers' compensation, employee insurance, minimum wage and overtime, and processes any change only by formal contract amendment signed by authorised representatives of both parties. It remains responsible to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality of the services regardless of subcontractors, flows Section (3) paragraph I into every subcontract, and takes any action the Commission directs to enforce those provisions including sanctions for noncompliance. It maintains the E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding, the sworn affidavit that the firm does not knowingly employ unauthorised aliens, and certification that every assigned employee is eligible and authorised to work in the United States, and it complies with Executive Order 07-13. It keeps all working papers and records, makes them available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor during the term and for three years from final payment, withholds material and reports from public release without MHTC's representative's prior consent, protects confidential factual matters and notifies MHTC immediately of any request for confidential information, and takes no assignment, delegation or novation without prior written consent. It files the FFATA reporting required by 2 C.F.R. Part 170 and holds General Liability of at least $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Automobile Liability at the same limits, and a Missouri workers' compensation policy, providing certificates before contract signing if asked. It also runs the minority and women hiring and MBE/WBE subcontracting participation effort, targeting 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation.

items.text: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) issued RFP TR202504, "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions", coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division.
items.reason: Letter states MHTC requests proposals for TR202504, coordinated by Research Unit of Construction and Materials Division.

items.text: The study is performed for MHTC and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), whose fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30.
items.reason: S8.1 names MHTC and MoDOT; S10.1 gives July 1 - June 30 fiscal year.

items.text: MHTC must describe realty rights it acquires or conveys by the metes and bounds method unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
items.reason: S9.1 states metes and bounds requirement, with exception for entire acquisition and last deed of record wording.

items.text: Property descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2 and must be reviewed by a professional land surveyor before the deed is presented to the grantor.
items.reason: S9.1 cites EPG 236.4.6.2 and surveyor review before presenting deed to grantor.

items.text: The business driver is to determine whether AI and Machine Learning can produce a "first draft" legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters that MoDOT's Right of Way staff could review and edit.
items.reason: S9.1 goal matches: AI/ML first draft LLD using MHTC parameters, reviewed and edited by ROW staff.

items.text: MoDOT's current LLD drafting is a manual, surveyor-reviewed process, so the RFP is seeking to reduce the drafting effort borne by Right of Way staff.
items.reason: Surveyor review and 'long and tedious' are stated; 'manual' process and goal of reducing ROW staff effort are not stated.

items.text: The client wants a research study, TR202504, on using AI/ML to write legal land descriptions, delivered under a contract period of 15 months.
items.reason: S8.1 gives study TR202504 for MHTC/MoDOT; S11.1 gives 15-month contract period.

items.text: The scope comprises six tasks: project management, literature review, MoDOT-provided LLD examples and program approval, a proof of concept that AI/ML can draft LLDs, training and a user manual, and draft and final reports with a research summary and presentation.
items.reason: Cited sources cover Tasks 1, 2, 3a-3c, 4, 5, 6 matching the listed scope; grouping into six tasks is fair.

items.text: The Offeror must demonstrate the technology creating draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and providing improvement feedback.
items.reason: S23.1 states exactly this demonstration and MoDOT review and feedback.

items.text: Deliverables include a data management plan, meeting agendas and minutes, a demonstration of AI writing a legal land description, ROW staff training, a user manual, and draft and final reports with a 1-2 page research summary and a presentation.
items.reason: S14.1 and S26.1 together list all these deliverables including 1-2 page summary and presentation.

items.text: The project timeline presumes a start of November 1, 2024, with a kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024 and the final report, summary, presentation and user manual due 1/1/2026.
items.reason: Start date, kick-off date, and final deliverables date all stated in cited sources.

items.text: The contract ends 2/2/2026, when the final invoice is due.
items.reason: Table states final invoice due and contract ends 2/2/2026.

items.text: Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, and the Offeror must submit a cost estimate on the Section (4) Price Page covering salaries, benefits, operating expense, F&A cost, miscellaneous and total.
items.reason: Cap of $175,000 and price page expense categories are both stated.

items.text: Questions or comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. (Central), and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is cause for disqualification.
items.reason: Email, date, time, and disqualification for other contact methods are stated.

items.text: Proposals must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 8/21/2024 at 10 a.m. (Central), and a proposal is not considered submitted until notification of receipt is received.
items.reason: Email, date, time, and receipt notification condition are stated in cited sources.

items.text: MoDOT will notify submitters about project selection, or about interviews to finalize selection, on 9/18/2024.
items.reason: Notification of selection or interviews on 9/18/2024 is stated.

items.text: Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, evaluated after a responsiveness determination against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee, with MHTC also entitled to consider historic information.
items.reason: Best proposal, responsiveness, TAC criteria, and MHTC historic information right are all stated.

items.text: The Work Plan must be narrative style, no longer than ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.
items.reason: Narrative style, ten pages, 12-point font, and MoDOT approval authority all stated.

items.text: The proposal must be one combined PDF in a set order, must identify experience in the requested services over the past three (3) years, and must name at least three client references from the past three years.
items.reason: Single combined PDF with order, three-year experience, and three references all stated.

items.text: The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs on 4/25/2025, deliver training and a manual by 7/25/2025, complete the interim presentation by 9/15/2025, and submit the draft final report, summary and user manual by 11/3/2025.
items.reason: All four milestone dates and deliverables match the table.

items.text: Applications must be web based and built on approved technologies, using .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8 or above), the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework, and approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use.
items.reason: Python approved-use is accurate, but 'must be web based' overstates source's 'should be'; also .NET Framework 'supported 4.8' fine. Web-based is only 'should'.

items.text: On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server, with Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher allowed only if approved by the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team.
items.reason: Source says SQL Server 2016 or higher only 'in certain cases' if approved; 'Oracle or latest SQL Server' is fine, but 'only' framing and details mostly match.

items.text: No Personal Identifiable Information may be stored in any database table without a specific business need and approval from the IS Cyber Security Team, and all web applications must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508.
items.reason: PII and accessibility requirements match S73.2.

items.text: Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management.
items.reason: Matches the third-party tools licensing clause in S73.1.

items.reason: Kick-off 11/15/2024 is stated, and the schedule says key milestone dates will be determined at kick-off, showing ambiguity.

items.reason: S9.1 has no 4/25/2025 demonstration or accuracy-threshold statement; only the draft reviewed by ROW staff is stated.

items.reason: S23.1 says demonstration on a variety of properties without specifying number or types; ten properties is a position.

items.reason: Training and user manual are required, but class size, format and copies are unspecified, so assumption fills a gap.

items.reason: Source cites EPG Section 236.4.6.2 requirements; the rule-set source and divergence handling are bidder positions, not misstated facts.

items.reason: Sources refer to Publication Guidelines and template on website without specifying location or version; the assumption resolves that.

items.text: Contract term conflicts with the dated milestone schedule. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes the final invoice at 2/2/2026, which is roughly 15 months from a 11/1/2024 start but only about 12 months from a later award or kick-off. If the term is measured from contract execution rather than the presumed 11/1/2024 start, the 4/25/2025 demonstration, 7/25/2025 training and 1/1/2026 final deliverables compress into a much shorter window than the price assumes. The bidder could be held to fixed dates it cannot resource, or be paid for a shorter period than the work needs. The dates are fixed in the milestone table while the term is stated separately, and the RFP does not say which governs; a slip in award date would leave the whole schedule unachievable at the priced effort.
items.reason: 15-month term, 2/2/2026 invoice and milestones are stated; the 11/1/2024 start and 12-month figure are not in sources.

items.text: No accuracy threshold for the AI/ML first draft. The RFP requires MoDOT Right of Way staff to review and edit the AI/ML draft but sets no accuracy target or tolerable edit effort. The bidder therefore cannot prove success, and MoDOT could judge the proof of concept unsuccessful on a standard the bidder never saw, putting the 7/25/2025 training milestone and final acceptance at risk. Acceptance of the core deliverable turns on an undefined measure; the proposed solution substitutes edit effort and error type per property, which MoDOT has not agreed to.
items.reason: Staff review and no accuracy threshold are supported; the 7/25/2025 training milestone is not among cited sources.

items.text: MHTC parameters undefined and assumed to arrive as structured data. The RFP treats the MHTC parameters as the input basis for the draft but does not define them or say in what form they will be supplied. The proposed solution assumes MoDOT delivers them as structured data at kick-off and does not build a parameter-capture interface; if they arrive as scanned plans, narrative deeds or not at all, the prototype needs an unplanned data-preparation layer. The whole drafting pipeline depends on an input the RFP does not specify, and the solution's assumption removes the fallback of capturing parameters in the tool.
items.reason: MHTC parameters used without definition or input format stated; remaining content is bidder solution and judgment.

items.text: LLD development program approval gate before Task 3c. MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named LLD development program before proof-of-concept work proceeds, and the RFP does not say what the submission must contain or how long approval takes. The solution assumes a commercial large-language-model service accessed through an approved API; if approval is refused or delayed, Task 3c stalls and the 4/25/2025 demonstration slips. A hard approval gate sits on the critical path to a fixed demonstration date, and the approval criteria and turnaround are not stated in the RFP.
items.reason: Approval gate is supported; the 4/25/2025 demonstration date is not in cited sources, nor is missing approval criteria.

items.text: Referenced exhibits and forms are not in the RFP. Exhibit A and Exhibit B are cited in the agreement requirements but are not in the document, and the Proposal Submission Form, Price Page, Standard Research Agreement, Publication Guidelines and the letter's Attachment are only available from the MoDOT website. If any of these carries a form, affidavit or term the bidder has not seen, the proposal can be non-responsive or the price can omit a required obligation. Missing exhibits include sworn affidavits and the price page, both of which are pass/fail submittal items, and the RFP does not reproduce them.
items.reason: Exhibit B, forms and website items supported; Exhibit A, letter's Attachment and pass/fail status are not in cited sources.

items.text: Fixed $175,000 cap against an open-ended scope. The RFP caps the work at $175,000 not-to-exceed but leaves the literature review scope, training audience, user manual content, number of quarterly meetings and demonstration size undefined. The solution prices a specific set of assumptions for each; if MoDOT expects more, the bidder absorbs the overrun because the cap does not move. Several cost drivers are unpriced in the RFP and the cap is fixed, so any expansion of scope comes directly out of the bidder's margin.
items.reason: $175,000 cap, literature review and training supported; quarterly meetings and demonstration size not shown in cited sources.

items.text: Milestone dates may be reset at kick-off. The milestone table fixes the demonstration, training, interim presentation, draft and final report dates, but the kick-off row says key milestone dates will be determined from the kick-off meeting. If MoDOT resets the dates at kick-off, the fixed-date price and resourcing plan no longer hold, and the bidder carries the cost of re-planning or of holding a team on standby. The RFP contains both a fixed table and a statement that dates are set at kick-off, so the binding schedule is genuinely unsettled until MoDOT answers.
items.reason: Table dates and kick-off row stating key milestone dates will be determined at the meeting are both in S15.2; the rest is risk judgment.

items.text: Demonstration property set and source data not specified. The RFP requires a demonstration on a variety of properties but does not say how many, which types, or what data MoDOT will supply. The solution prices ten properties spanning whole-parcel, partial-take and easement acquisitions on MoDOT-supplied data; if MoDOT supplies more properties, different types or incomplete plans, the proof of concept effort and the 4/25/2025 date are at risk. The demonstration is a fixed-date deliverable whose effort is driven entirely by a property count the RFP leaves open.
items.reason: RFP requires demonstration on a variety of properties, no count or data specified in sources; 4/25/2025 date is cited. Solution details are the bidder's position.

items.text: Python approval gate could block the AI/ML build. The RFP reserves Python for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses, with larger use requiring Information Systems Best Practices Review Team approval. The solution assumes its Python work stays below that threshold; if the ML pipeline needs substantial Python, the design must be reworked into C#/.NET or wait for an approval of unstated duration, delaying the build. The threshold for large-scale Python use is undefined, and the solution's assumption that it stays below it is untested against the actual model work.
items.reason: Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small uses; large-scale needs BRPT approval; C#/.NET approved. Threshold undefined in sources.

items.text: Oracle 19C and SQL Server requirements conflict. The RFP makes Oracle 19C mandatory for on-premise databases while also allowing Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval. The solution proposes Oracle 19C only and assumes no approval is needed; if MoDOT's hosting environment is SQL Server-based, the bidder either pays for an Oracle licence and DBA effort or waits for an approval that may not come. The two database requirements point in different directions and the RFP does not settle which platform MoDOT will host, so the choice turns on facts the RFP does not give.
items.reason: Sources offer Oracle 19C or SQL Server as alternatives, not mandatory Oracle; the 'conflict' and 'mandatory' framing misstates them.

items.text: Two pages of the RFP could not be read. Pages 19 and 20 carry almost no extractable text and are dominated by an image block, so requirements or forms on those pages may be invisible to the bid team. If those pages set a deliverable, a format rule or a mandatory form, the proposal could miss it and be scored down or rejected. The pages fall in the scope-of-work section where task requirements are set, and the bid team cannot confirm what they contain from the text alone.

Accessibility and PII obligations underestimated. The web application must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, and no PII may be stored without IS Cyber Security Team approval. The RFP does not supply the state standard or the approval procedure, and the solution treats accessibility as a lead role rather than a tested deliverable; remediation late in the build would consume the four-week adjustment window before the 7/25/2025 training. Accessibility conformance is a mandatory technical requirement with an external standard the bidder does not hold, and the schedule leaves only four weeks between demonstration and training.
items.reason: WCAG and PII/approval facts are supported; four-week window between demonstration and training is not stated, and 'State standard not supplied' is unsupported.
